Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

even adverb

adding something unexpected

also even more, even bigger, even if (see even if)

classical

Publ. E 13: Etiam capillus ūnus habet umbram suam.
Plin. Ep. 6.20.18: sōl etiam effulsit
Traupman 310

etiam

adverb, before or after the word it stresses

Also with comparatives, “even more”: etiam dēterius quam soleō, even worse than usual (Cic. Fam. 5.14.1). “Not even” is nē … quidem.

Other words

  • vel — even (if you like)

    adverb: with superlatives, and “even” of something one may choose · also used · classical · Quint. 10.7.25: vel sōlī tamen dīcāmus potius quam omnīnō nōn dīcāmus; Cic. Att. 7.10.1: crēbrō ad mē scrībe vel quod in buccam vēnerit

    “Even, if you like”: vel quod in buccam vēnerit, even whatever comes into your head; with a superlative, “the very”: vel maximus (Lewis & Short).

  • et — even, also

    adverb, before the word it stresses · also used · classical · Tac. Agr. 9.7: aliquandō et ēlēgit

    See also.

Examples

  • Etiam capillus ūnus habet umbram suam.

    Even a single hair has its own shadow.Publ. E 13

  • mox diēs vērus; sōl etiam effulsit

    soon it was real daylight; the sun even shone outPlin. Ep. 6.20.18

  • Etiam sānātō vulnere cicātrīx manet.

    Even when the wound has healed, the scar remains.Ps.-Publ. E 12

  • vel sōlī tamen dīcāmus potius quam omnīnō nōn dīcāmus

    let us speak even alone rather than not speak at allQuint. 10.7.25

  • tū, quaesō, crēbrō ad mē scrībe vel quod in buccam vēnerit

    please write to me often, even whatever comes into your headCic. Att. 7.10.1

See also also, not even, even if.
